steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Texture describes how musical lines combine: monophonic (single line), homophonic (melody + chords), polyphonic (independent lines), antiphonal (spatially separated groups). | Key Fact: Sonority (timbre) is the unique sound quality of each instrument or voice — same notes sound different on violin vs clarinet vs voice. | Key Fact: Dynamics shape musical expression: crescendo builds intensity; diminuendo releases it; sudden changes (sfz) create drama and surprise. | Key Fact: Instrumental techniques change sonority: arco (bowed) vs pizzicato (plucked) on strings; con sordino (muted) brass; palm mute on guitar; falsetto voice.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how dynamics texture and sonority are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use dynamics texture and sonority. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use dynamics texture and sonority in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
